chunks: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah created Adam and granted him the world as an allotted domain. So whatever belonged to Adam (عليه السلام) belongs to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and whatever belonged to the Messenger of Allah belongs to the Imams from the family of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.آدَمَ: Adam عليه السلام, the first human and recipient of the initial divine allotment
key_terms.آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: the family of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله, from whom the Imams are
key_terms.أَقْطَعَهُ: granted him as an allotted possession or domain
key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the worldly realm granted by Allah
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةِ: the Imams, the divinely designated successors from the family of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.خَلَقَ: created; denotes Allah’s act of originating Adam
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, to whom Adam’s entitlement is said to pass
key_terms.قَطِيعَةً: an allotted portion, grant, or assigned domain

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the world’s divinely granted authority passing from Adam عليه السلام to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and the Imams عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Allah granted Adam a divinely allotted domain in the world, and that this authority and entitlement passed to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and then to the Imams from آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وآله. It expresses a theological vision of divinely designated authority and inheritance centered on the Prophet and the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.
